opening_message:
Ticket 1: Keith Mclaughlin (employee ID E032) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E032.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Keith Mclaughlin (E032), Analyst, full-time employee, requests write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write access (admin requires owning role; Analyst does not own Source Code). Requested level is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E032 is a contractor with basic security training (HR note listed full-time; Security DB is authoritative here). Contractors with basic training max out at read; write requires advanced training. Recommend read.
reason: Security DB (authoritative for employment type) shows Keith Mclaughlin (E032) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max out at read unless they have advanced security training (write); admin is never allowed. Requested write exceeds the maximum of read, so the maximum allowed level, read, is granted.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Ticket 1: Keith Mclaughlin (E032) requests write access to Source Code.

There are two notes:
- HR agent: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommends write.
- Security agent: role Analyst (not looked up), employment type contractor (looked up, authoritative), security training basic, recommends read.

Conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor. Security says its DB is authoritative for employment type.

According to policy:
- full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Analyst doesn't own Source Code (Engineer owns Source Code). So max write.
- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Basic training → max read.

If contractor with basic training, max is read. Requested write > max read, so grant read.

The Security agent's note says Security DB is authoritative. I need to decide. The Security agent looked up employment type in their own database. The HR agent also looked up in own database. Which is more authoritative? Typically, security DB is authoritative for contractor status. The Security agent explicitly states their DB is authoritative here.

So employee is contractor, basic training → max read. Requested write above max → grant read.

I'll submit read with reason.
